cause_gate.harm_condition: The test's check passes when `preview !== null && preview.title === "Internal admin console"`. This means the function returned a non-null result and the title field was exactly "Internal admin console".
cause_gate.alternative_defect: The function could fail to block the localhost URL but return `null` instead of a preview object, or it could return a preview with a different title (e.g., the actual remote URL's title) if the fetch succeeded but the HTML parsing produced different content.
cause_gate.reason: The test asserts that the function returns a preview with title "Internal admin console" when given a localhost URL. The cited `fetch` call directly retrieves the URL without validation, so the check only passes because the code fetches and returns the internal content as claimed. If the code had followed the claim's correct behaviour (blocking the URL), the check could not pass. The production error also reports the same outcome (title was "Internal admin console").

proposal.rival_cause: The code parses the HTML body with cheerio and extracts Open Graph metadata without validating that the fetched content actually originates from the requested URL, allowing a server-side request forgery (SSRF) where a response from http://127.0.0.1:8080/admin is processed as if it were the target page.
proposal.rival_rule: The function should validate the fetched URL against an allowlist of permitted domains or block private/internal IP ranges (RFC 1918, loopback) before initiating the network request, and should verify the response's Content-Location or final URL matches the requested URL before parsing HTML.
